top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B038) credits a distinct, mature conceptual step. It moved trade analysis from countries and industries to heterogeneous firms and added selection and reallocation channels for the gains from trade. That mechanism has been tested directly on firm-level customs and production data for more than twenty years. The two-name credit set follows the core model and the broader firm-level agenda closely. A citation worded around the mechanism, not any welfare magnitude, fits the evidence. The main residual risk is the claims of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum. I regard the 2008 trade prize as a separate discovery. P002 (B015) comes next on influence and maturity, but its attribution is contested and the micro evidence on Calvo pricing is mixed. P004 follows because its two-name attribution is clean, though its direct identification is weaker and it overlaps thematically with the 2022 prize. P003 has strong identification, but its boundary between two strands and the choice of third name are unsettled. Any credible award ranks above no award (P000).
recusal_note: No tie to Melitz, Helpman, Redding or the credited names on the other proposals is apparent from the profile. Disclosed only: I share an SSE affiliation with committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg. I gave the 2020 presentation speech, which may bias me toward applied, implementation-linked work. My field of matching, auctions and mechanism design is adjacent to information design, which was my opening first choice. These ties are not adjudicated.
